::: {.why}
Milestone 6 is eight of these side by side, and generating them from the result object means they cannot drift from what the code actually did.
:::

## What you should be able to do tonight

- Generate a standard one-page summary per signal directly from its result object.
- Have the rationale, the trial count and the capacity assumptions on the page rather than in your head.

## Tasks <span class='task-total'>60 min</span>

::: {.task-list}
::: {.task}
<input type="checkbox" class="task-check"> [40 min]{.task-min} Build the report generator in qlib/signals/report.py: rationale from the docstring, IC and decay curve, quantile returns with monotonicity, information ratio with an interval, turnover, capacity with assumptions, the net-Sharpe-against-cost chart, the trial count from research_log.jsonl, and the position of the result in the null distribution. One page, generated.
:::
::: {.task}
<input type="checkbox" class="task-check"> [20 min]{.task-min} Generate all four and read them as a stranger would. Anything that requires you to explain it verbally is missing from the page, and fixing that now is what makes milestone 6 readable in February.
:::
:::

## The running strategy

::: {.project}
qlib/signals/report.py generates the standard one-page signal summary from the result object. Milestone 6 becomes an assembly of generated pages rather than a document that can disagree with the code.
:::
